analysis: All three changed files are test-only Swift sources under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. The changes: (1) EngineV2BenchmarkMTPVerificationTests.swift line 48 and EngineV2ContiguousAdmissionTests.swift line 21 and EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift line 74 qualify Gemma4TextConfiguration as MLXLLM.Gemma4TextConfiguration, which resolves a type-name ambiguity and is behavior-neutral. (2) EngineV2BenchmarkMTPVerificationTests.swift line 53 updates the OtherTarget stub's LanguageModel.prepare signature to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters), which tracks an upstream mlx-swift-lm API change. That protocol-signature change matches a dependency bump whose production-side adoption is outside the supplied evidence. I found no change to production code, coordinator/provider wire handling, attestation, key custody, prefix-cache crypto, SSD tier gating, TTL, HMAC lookup, admission, or KV budget logic. The tests still assert existing security-relevant invariants unchanged: benchmark scope refusal when the prefix cache is enabled or there is no production grant, rejection of conflicting drafters, and contiguous admission refusing oversize prompts. No assertions were weakened. The threat model entries touching this area, T-041 (prefix cache) and TB-007 (inference engine), are not affected by these edits. Remaining integration question: the dependency update behind the new prepare signature (state/prefill parameters) may change prefill or cache behavior in production code or in the vendored mlx-swift-lm, which was not supplied here and should be reviewed where it lands. This is not a finding in the test files.
